title: Keep audit repair probes executable without nesting the full test runner
detail: The audit itself introduced eight ledger commands that spawned Vitest again inside the backlog sweep, regressing LIVE-034 and duplicating normal CI. Replace those commands with direct assertions against actual code/fixtures: rejected draft writes/bin action and unsafe write/load/list routes; all six outbox state-write failure branches; impossible event dates; real React city-search races and filter preservation; actual sitemap/page-wrapper eligibility; cached census reads and real isolated budget control/mutants; actual quota resolver with synthetic gh/sleep/date and cleanup. No application assertion is waived, and all fuller Vitest suites remain normal CI inputs. Seven independent controls substitute the original main source for the repaired module or fixture and each fails as expected; the fixed direct probes pass. Root test suite, native suite and browser evidence stay separately labelled. The cost consequence remains the existing backlog-contract test, rather than recursively running the guard from its own row.

verify.note: The merged ledger must retain executable existing direct consequences for all eight repairs and must not reintroduce nested suite runners. Actual full backlog cost is verified by the existing standalone contract test, never recursively here.
